comparator.name: Bachelor Mechanical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: TU Delft's live 2026-2027 study guide, checked 2026-10-03, identifies BSc Werktuigbouwkunde (B-WB, CROHO 56966) as a three-year, 180-EC programme and publishes its complete current curriculum. Years one and two each contain ten 6-EC courses. Year three contains a genuine 30-EC minor plus 6 EC Systems and Control, 6 EC Integrated Mechanical Systems, 4 EC Engineer and Society and a 14-EC Bachelor Final Project. The component list below therefore preserves every published course and all 180 EC without selecting an invented route or minor.
components: Genuine first-semester minor space preserved from the official curriculum.

exception.reason: TU Delft Mechanical Engineering is an integrated engineering sequence in statics, mechanics of materials, dynamics, thermodynamics, advanced mechanics, materials science, fluid flow and heat transfer, process engineering, signals, systems and control, robotics and integrated mechanical systems. Four consecutive first-year design projects and three further second-year engineering projects culminate in a 14-EC mechanical-engineering final project. UCR offers useful mathematics, programming, product-design and sustainability courses, but it does not offer the mechanical-science core, engineering laboratory and workshop progression, or cumulative mechanical design and research sequence on which the degree depends. A 24-course response would be an applied mathematics, computing and sustainable-design programme, not Mechanical Engineering.
exception.curriculumContext: The live 2026-27 study guide accounts for all 180 EC. Year one is 60 EC across mathematics, statics, mechanics of materials, dynamics, thermodynamics and four design projects. Year two is 60 EC across further mathematics, signals and systems, materials science, advanced mechanics, fluid flow and heat, process engineering and thermodynamics, plus advanced-design, robotics and materials projects. Year three preserves 30 EC of genuine minor space and requires Systems and Control Engineering, Integrated Mechanical Systems, Engineer and Society and a 14-EC Bachelor Final Project. No named graduation route requires selection.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide relevant quantitative tools, while DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming adds computing. BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design covers customer needs, fabrication planning, prototyping and sustainability; ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design address environmental impact and sustainable energy-system assessment. The workbook nevertheless contains no statics or mechanics-of-materials course; no thermodynamics, fluid-mechanics or heat-transfer sequence; no engineering materials, manufacturing-process, elasticity, tribology, mechanical dynamics, robotics, mechatronics or finite-element course; and no mechanical-engineering laboratory, workshop, integrated design-project or bachelor-research sequence. The adjacent courses cannot supply a coherent 23-course non-PPD mechanical-engineering pathway.
